meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.name: Macronutrient ratio
data.description: Ratio of protein:carbohydrate:fat in the diet; affects mTOR activation independently of total caloric intake.
data.description_beginner: The balance of protein, carbohydrate, and fat in the diet. Changing this ratio can switch mTOR activity up or down independently of how many total calories are eaten.

studies.title: The ratio of macronutrients, not caloric intake, dictates cardiometabolic health, aging, and longevity in ad libitum-fed mice

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Lifespan and cardiometabolic health were determined not by caloric intake but by the protein:carbohydrate ratio; a low protein ratio was associated with lower hepatic mTOR activation.
